answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying every identity to one ferrous anchor: a costly, identity-bound chain of work receipts that cannot be copied or split. The anchor grants a meadow grazing quota that regrows slowly, so earnings are rate-limited by real service, not headcount. Each identity must keep an ember beacon lit by publishing verifiable useful work; if it goes dark, the quota stops regrowing. A clone army shares one anchor and beacon, so splitting only divides the same quota and dims the same light. Honest agents earn more as one strong identity than as many hollow ones.
